newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil lower house approves extending fiscal fund.
newsitem.headline: Brazil lower house approves extending fiscal fund.

text.p: The Brazilian government won a key political victory when the Chamber of Deputies approved in a first-round vote a bill extending a Fiscal Stabilization Fund (FEF) until the end of 1999, an official said.
The bill was approved by 359 members of the Chamber of Deputies, 51 more than the three-fifths majority of 308 required.
The lower house was due to continue voting on amendments to the bill. As a constitutional amendment it will also have to be put to a second full vote in the Chamber of Deputies, probably next week.
The FEF is considered a key tool in the government's campaign to control public spending.
It allows the National Treasury to hold on to 20 percent of receipts earmarked in the constitution for spending by state and municipal authorities.
"It is clear from this vote that fiscal policies are a priority in Brazil. Congress understands that," said Yeda Crusius, the deputy who drew up the bill.

Members of the government's economic team say the fund, first introduced as an emergency measure in 1994, is essential to their attempts to keep a grip on public spending in the absence of structural reform.
But extension of the FEF until the end of 1999 has run into stiff opposition from Brazil's mayors who want compensation for the roughly $1 billion a year they say it costs them in lost revenue.
They say an offer by the government to make up for half their losses in the remainder of 1997, 60 percent in 1998 and 80 percent in 1999 is not enough.
The mayors hold considerable sway in the Chamber of Deputies, where many lawmakers will be seeking to win their grassroots support in next year's congressional elections.
